reading:
What the judges love in this line is one idea and three instruments. The idea is that the day of the month is one light numeral that does several jobs. It sits in the waypoint ring on the route, leads each Coming up row and heads each month cell, so the figure and the list read as one thing with no legend. Interaction (8) called it "the best comprehension device in the heat" and usability called it "the best date scan". Type called it "real calendar typesetting". The three instruments are the readout strip (label, dotted leader, right-aligned tabular figure, which type would make the system's figure standard), the arcing flight plan with its lit leg to Next, and the needle meter on Status. Feedback gave it 8.4 and 7.9 for carrying the owner's brief page by page: bone on slate, amber only for late, phosphor only on what is live.

What sank it, from 7.40 down to 7.46 on the landing panel (#8 of 16), was mostly fixable execution:
- The pilot-lamp ticks. Round, and amber with a minus when late, they read as radios, "no-entry" or "remove" signs. Six lenses said so twice, and the tour's lessons list it as a FAILED REACH.
- Two faces for one mark: the rings in Plex Mono 500, the rows in Plex Sans 300 (five lenses).
- Boxes inside boxes. Bays wrap read-only lists, and amber slabs and inverted-green chips ('Fri 2 Oct', 'Working') read as editor-theme glare.
- An empty strip right of the Coming up rows, wordy placards, and a crowded Status head.
- Soul's complaint that the greeting and readout strip are matte where the original glowed. A plain headline, with the first thing seen unlit.
- On the phone the readout strip falls below the first screen, and Home takes three stacked bands to reach To do.

Since these crossing rounds set it beside Desk Terminal, Joined, its bar is now page-template coherence. That means one head row per page, light that does a job, matte rows on the ground, and controls that look like controls.

What would make it win: keep the numeral-in-the-ring law and the route, and fix every control. Then take from the main camp the structure that removes its box-heaviness (Backlit Plate's engraved rule heads) and the page head the panel named its standard (Quote Board's title plus figure plus stacked unit). From Joined, take the lit NOW line that joins To do to the route's Now. From Dessau, take a shape law that turns 'one control, one look' into a rule for every page. Then relight the phosphor where it lives: the Next ring and leg, Today and Late on the readout strip, a pool under the greeting. The result is a flight console whose lamps are true instruments and whose family rows are plain and ruled.

briefs.name: Waypoint, Ruled
briefs.hypothesis: Waypoint Lamps lost points on execution, not on its idea: round lamp ticks, two faces for one numeral, bays inside bays, inverted chips, wordy placards and a matte greeting. Every judge who scored it praised the numeral-in-the-ring law and the readout strip. This cross clears all of those faults. It also takes the main camp's page structure: Backlit Plate's engraved rule heads in place of the bays, Quote Board's head row on every inner page, and Joined's lit NOW line on To do. Dessau's shape law (ring = light, square = the family's, bar = the page, triangle = needs a look) turns 'one control, one look' into a page-wide rule. The result keeps the most legible instrument in either camp and reaches Joined's page-template coherence. With the light restored on the Next ring, the leg, Today, Late and the greeting pool, it should also recover the soul points the landing panel withheld.
briefs.brief:
Start from t3-console-graft: copy /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/x14a-b/palettes/t3-console-graft.json and variants/t3-console-graft/ (sheet.css plus templates). The route, the waypoint rings, the hop rows, the readout strip, the Status meter, the radar Next up tube and the slate ground all stay. Recognisable at a glance: same bar, same Home order (greeting with tube, then the readout strip, then Coming up with the arcs and day-numeral rows), same bone route on slate.

SYSTEM RULE: the shape law, written at the top of sheet.css and keyed in the footer.
- A RING (circle) is LIGHT or a waypoint. It is used for the route's rings, the lamps in the readout strip and on Status, the Next up tube's power dot, the mark, and today's ring on the month. A ring is never pressed.
- A SQUARE is THE FAMILY'S. It is used for their checkboxes, fields, kind swatches and the date leaves on Plans. Every square can be pressed or typed in.
- A BAR is THE PAGE'S OWN. It is used for the rule heads' 3px lead, the current place in the nav (2px top bar, already there), buttons, and the 3px row edge.
- A small TRIANGLE (clip-path) is NEEDS A LOOK. It is used for late, the setup step and Status 'Needs a look'. It is always amber, always beside words, never alone.
- Footer, in base.html beside the tagline: `.foot-key` with four 11px keys and words: '◯ lit', '▢ yours', '▬ the page', '△ needs a look'. Set them in Plex Sans 500 12.5px, sentence case, in var(--faint). Do not use Dessau's tracked caps.

1. TICKS ARE SQUARES. Rebuild `button.tick::before`, `.task-box` and `input:is([type=checkbox])::before` (sheet.css ~L520-531) as a 24px square well: background var(--field), 1.5px border #6b7772, radius 4px, inside a 44px hit area.
- Hover and :focus-visible preview a faint check at 35% opacity.
- Checked fills the square with var(--brand) and a #07130c 2px check (SVG mask), with a 6px brand halo.
- Late is never drawn in the box. A late row keeps its 3px amber left edge (`.is-late`), and its 'was due 5 days ago' words are in amber with a 9px amber triangle before them.
- The same square goes on the form's 'Needs booking', the ask box's 'Send where I am' and the controls sheet.
- In tasks.html, add 'Tick when done' as the head of the tick column (12.5px, var(--label)).
- Change 'Called off' to 'Cancelled' everywhere (tasks.html Show tabs).

2. ONE FACE FOR THE NUMERAL. The ring numerals in home.html `.stop-n` and in plans_month.html move from Plex Mono 500 to the row's face: IBM Plex Sans, font-variant-numeric tabular-nums lining-nums, at 500 in the ring (15px) and 300 at the row's head (`.hop-day`, 40px). This is one family; the weight changes only with size. Month cells use the same face at 300, 22px.

3. BAYS OFF, RULES ON (Backlit Plate's rule heads). Every block that is only read leaves its slate bay and sits on the page ground under an engraved rule head. This covers Coming up, To do, Lately added, the kids' wishes, and Status's three columns.
- The rule head (`.rule`, replacing `.section-head` inside `.bay`): a 3px x 40px bone lead bar (#b9b29c), 12px gap, then the title.
- The title is an h2 in Plex Sans Condensed 600, 22px, var(--heading).
- After the title, a 1px groove line (#2c3533 over a #000 1px shadow, so it reads engraved) runs flex:1 to the right.
- At the right end comes the figure and its link: '4 plans · All plans →' as `.rule-fig` (Plex Sans 450, 14px, var(--dim)). Its count is tabular, and late counts are amber words, e.g. '4 open · 3 late · All →'. The figure is never boxed.
- The welcome stays a slate panel, because it is the cockpit: the one bay on Home. The Next up tube keeps its case.
- Bays survive only around controls: the To do filter rack and forms.

4. HOME, top to bottom.
(a) THE GREETING. The title is 'Give Vera something to *plan*.'
- Set it in Plex Sans Condensed 600 at clamp(2.25rem, 1.4rem + 2.6vw, 3.25rem) with line-height 1.02, in var(--heading). Only 'plan' is lit, with E1's two-layer halo. The full stop is in the same run.
- On the phone it breaks as 'Give Vera / something to plan.' (a `<wbr>`-free natural break at 390px). Check that 'plan.' never orphans.
- The title moves out of the box frame to stand above it, so the box's top edge is free.
- The ask box keeps its frame. Placeholder unchanged.
- Behind the greeting, put E7's greeting-glow, scanlines and all: radial 13% brand from the bottom-left plus a 7% wash top-right, on `.welcome.console`. It spills a 70px green pool down onto the readout strip's top edge (soul's 'first thing seen is lit').
- Starters keep 8px gaps.
(b) THE READOUT STRIP, now part of the welcome's foot (style asked to merge it). The cells are Today, Plans, To do, Late and Ideas.
- Each cell is an `<a>` with a 44px minimum height, leading to /plans, /tasks, /tasks?show=open (late rows first), and /ideas.
- Today becomes the bone date 'Fri 2 Oct' in Plex Mono, with a breathing 8px brand lamp before it (E20). No inverted chip.
- The Late figure '3' is amber with a 6px amber halo.
- The Plans, To do and Ideas figures are bone, matte.
- Leaders are 1px dotted in #3a4441, capped so a cell never exceeds 15rem.
- On the phone (≤40rem) the strip becomes a 2-row grid placed directly under the title and above the box, so the counts are on the first screen. The tube follows the box.
(c) THE NEXT UP TUBE. Keep it as is. Its placard becomes one line, the machine's status foot taken from Joined: '● Ready · OpenAI · gpt-6-luna · Status →' (see 6).
(d) SETUP. One line under the greeting, not a slab: an amber 9px triangle, then 'Finish setting up', then the steps left as a bone figure '3', then the next step as one link, then 'All the setup steps →' at the right. It has a 2px steel left bar and no amber fill, so amber stays for late.
(e) COMING UP, under its rule head ('Coming up ——— 4 plans · All plans →').
- The arcs band is compressed to 72px total.
- The flown trail from Now to today is dotted #6b665a.
- The leg to Next is brand with the full halo (2px core, 6px bloom, 16px haze), and the Next ring breathes.
- The route ahead is cooled from tan to pewter-bone #c4c2b4 at 1.5px.
- The hatched weekend bands drop to 4% contrast.
- Rows span the full width in a grid: day numeral (stacked Oct/Sun) | time (mono 14px) | title, flex | a dotted leader | the relative column ('Next · in 2 days', 'in 7 days'), right-aligned at the row's end. The leader closes the gap after short titles.
- The Google note moves under the rows as one 13px line in var(--faint), with the plug icon.
- Every ring has its row, Next first and lit. The rings' numerals equal the rows'.
(f) TO DO and LATELY ADDED sit side by side under rule heads, on the ground.
- To do rows: square tick | title (16px 600) | who (dim) | due words right-aligned. Late rows have the amber edge and amber words.
- Joined's lit NOW line sits between the last late row and the first upcoming one (see 7).
- Lately added keeps its two-line stacks (title, then a kind word in the kind colour, 13px, on its own line). Its kind swatch becomes an 8px SQUARE.
(g) THE KIDS' WISHES: one ruled line, 'The kids' wishes ——— Maya 0 · Theo 0 · All →'.

5. EVERY INNER PAGE OPENS ON ONE HEAD ROW (Quote Board's device).
- `.page-head` holds `.title-row`: the h1 in Plex Sans Condensed 600 at clamp(2.4rem, 1.5rem + 2.6vw, 3.5rem), then the page's figure in Plex Sans Condensed 500 at the same size, tabular. The figure is bone #d9d2bb, not a section colour, never yellow.
- Next to the figure, a stacked two-line unit in Plex Mono 12.5px var(--label):
  - To do: 'Things to do 4' with 'open' over '△ 3 late', the late line an amber link to the late rows.
  - Plans: 'Plans 4' with 'still to come' over 'to 1 Nov'.
  - Ideas: 'Ideas 12' with 'ideas' over 'last added Sun 27 Sep'.
  - Status: 'Status 5' with 'working' over '△ 1 needs a look'.
  - Settings and the form get no figure.
- The one green primary sits at the right of the same row ('Add something to do', 'Add an idea'; Plans keeps its List/Month keys there).
- This replaces the head readout tiles on To do and Plans and the Ideas readout tiles (feedback: too small).
- The subtitle stays as one 16px line under the row.

6. THE MACHINE'S FOOT (Joined's status foot). Every tube's placard becomes the one-line foot:
- a breathing brand ring lamp, 'Ready' (Plex Sans 600), the model and the day's limit in Plex Mono var(--dim), and 'Status →' at the right;
- or, when there is trouble, an amber triangle and 'Needs a look'.
- Only Status's meter keeps a scale placard, cut to 'Spent today, against the $2.00 limit.'

7. TO DO PAGE (tasks.html).
- Head row as in 5.
- The crew filter is drawn as lamps: each person a 10px ring, amber-cored if they have late items, with the name and '2 late' in words.
- The search and the Show keys sit in one bay (the only one), sized to their content.
- Rows are on the ground under a rule head 'Open ——— up to 100 shown'.
- The lit NOW line (from Joined) runs between late and upcoming:
  - a full-width 1px line, brand at 45%, with an 8px breathing brand ring at the tick column;
  - 'NOW' in Plex Mono 500 12.5px, brand with a 0.45em halo;
  - a 1px pewter rail running down through the tick column above it, joining the boxes like stops before Now. It is the route's grammar on the list.
- Due column: the words on top ('Was due 5 days ago', amber) and the date under them in mono, with no invented clock time unless one was set (drop '19:56').
- The Edit keys stay 44px.

8. PLANS MONTH (plans_month.html).
- Today's cell carries a brand RING around the '2', not an inverted square.
- Plan days carry the row numeral in a pewter ring.
- The arc lines between cells:
  - the route ahead at 1.5px pewter-bone;
  - the flown trail fainter and dotted;
  - only the leg from today to Next lit, with the full halo.
- No rail runs across weeks with no plans.
- The event chips' round markers become 8px squares (the family's), with Next's chip keeping a brand edge.
- The head tube is replaced by the head row (5) plus Next as the first line of the month bay's head: 'Next · Sun 4 · Oaks Park roller rink', with the 4 in a lit ring.

9. STATUS (status.html).
- Head row as in 5, with the meter tube floated right at the same top line, so the head is not stacked.
- The 'Working', 'Off' and 'Needs a look' inverted mono tags go. Each register row is: a lamp (brand ring lit = working, 1.5px pewter hollow ring = off, amber triangle = needs a look), the item name, then a sentence-case dim word ('working', 'off', 'no key').
- The three columns sit on the ground under rule heads ('Who answers ——— 3 of 4 on').
- The meter keeps its needle, and gets a limit tick and a ghost peak (lesson r13).

10. CHAT, SETTINGS, IDEAS, FORM.
- Each takes the rule heads, the head row and the square ticks.
- Chat's flight-log spine keeps its lit last stop, and Vera's newest line gets less green fill (8% brand over slate).
- Ideas' filter rack becomes one row of latched keys above the list.
- Settings sections: rule heads, with the caution as the one-line triangle form.

Type steps, written as tokens on :root:
- --fs-label 12.5
- --fs-small 14
- --fs-body 16
- --fs-lead 18
- --fs-head 22 (rule heads)
- --fs-title clamp to 56 (page titles and the greeting)
- --fs-num 40 (the day numeral)

Faces: Plex Sans for body; Plex Sans Condensed for titles, heads and the head figure; Plex Mono only for times, dates in columns and the readout strip's labels; VT323 only on glass. No tracked caps on nav or buttons.

briefs.avoids:
It answers each criticism in turn.
- 'Ticked reads like a radio' and the 'amber minus reads as remove or no-entry' (interaction, usability, skeptic, system): square ticks, with late on the edge, the words and a triangle.
- 'Two faces for one mark' (five lenses): one Plex Sans numeral.
- 'Every block is a bay inside a bay, box-heavy' and 'stacked bands read dashboard-generic' (system, style): rule heads on the ground, with one bay left on Home.
- 'Empty ground right of the relative column' and 'the lonely calendar note': full-width rows, a leader and the note under the rows.
- 'Inverted-green Fri 2 Oct and Working tags are an editor-theme tic': lamps and plain words.
- 'Placards over-explain': one-line Ready foot.
- 'Amber left bars add up to a caution panel': amber on late only, and setup on a steel bar.
- 'Status head crowded': one head row with the meter at its right.
- 'The greeting is a plain headline, the readout strip matte where the original glowed' (soul): greeting pool, lit 'plan', lit Today and Late.
- 'Readout labels small', 'Ideas readout tiles small', 'Ideas filter panel oversized': the head row's figure and one row of latched keys.
- 'Readout below the phone's first screen' and 'three bands before To do' (interaction): strip under the title on the phone, and arcs at 72px.
- 'Arcs decoration a family must learn': every ring is a numbered row.
- 'Bone route reads tan': pewter-bone.
- 'Called off vs Cancelled'.
- Invented clock times: dropped.

WHAT IT KEEPS: the flight-plan arcs with numerals in the rings, the lit Next leg, the big day-numeral rows, the readout strip with leaders, the radar Next up tube, the Status needle meter, the flight-log chat spine, and the slate-and-bone palette with brand only on what is live.

WHAT IT GIVES UP to make room:
- the round pilot-lamp ticks (the graft's own signature);
- the slate bays around every read section;
- the engraved placards under each tube (now one status foot);
- the readout tiles in inner page heads;
- the Plans head tube (replaced by the head row and a lit Next line in the month head);
- the amber caution slab with its lamp block.
briefs.title:
'Give Vera something to *plan*.' It is new: no design in the main tournament, the tour or the crossing rounds has carried it (titles.md has only 'Anything to plan?' and the 'Tell Vera…' family).
- It says FamilyDB's job as an invitation to hand Vera anything: a weekend, a reminder, an idea to keep, a calendar entry. Each of those is 'something to plan', which suits the placeholder beneath it.
- It names who hears you, as the panel's favourite 'Tell Vera what to plan.' does, and lights the job word at the end where the eye stops.
- It avoids the faults the judges found in the line's own 'Tell Vera our plan.': 'our plan' presumes a plan already exists (interaction, type, skeptic), while 'something' invites what isn't planned yet.
- It is an imperative, not a question, so it cannot be heard as 'show me the plan' (six notes faulted the question forms). It cannot be answered 'no' either, unlike 'Anything to plan?'.
- The lit word is four letters, so the halo stays small.
- It sets on one desktop line at 56px condensed and on two phone lines ('Give Vera / something to plan.') with 'plan.' kept whole.
